question:
A 46-year-old male presents with a 4-month history of upper back pain localized to the right paraspinal
region, worsened by prolonged sitting. He denies any history of trauma, numbness, or weakness. His
past medical history is unremarkable, and he works as a security guard. On physical examination,
muscle strength, tone, and reflexes in the upper extremities are normal bilaterally, and sensation is
intact. The examination reveals restricted back flexion and a tender point on the T4 transverse process
on the right. The patient consents to osteopathic manipulative treatment. Which of the following
positions is most appropriate for counterstrain treatment? Answer Choices: (A) Flexed torso, sidebent
right, rotated right (B) Flexed torso, sidebent right, rotated left (C) Extended torso, sidebent right,
rotated left (D) Extended torso, sidebent right, rotated right (E) Extended torso, sidebent left, rotated
right (F) Extended torso, sidebent left, rotated left (G) Neutral torso, sidebent left, rotated right (H)
Neutral torso, sidebent right, rotated right (I) Flexed torso, sidebent left, rotated right (J) Extended
torso, sidebent left, rotated neutral

A. Extended torso, sidebent left, rotated right
B. Extended torso, sidebent left, rotated left
C. Flexed torso, sidebent right, rotated right
D. Extended torso, sidebent right, rotated right
E. Neutral torso, sidebent right, rotated right
F. Flexed torso, sidebent left, rotated right
G. Neutral torso, sidebent left, rotated right
H. Extended torso, sidebent right, rotated left
I. Extended torso, sidebent left, rotated neutral
J. Flexed torso, sidebent right, rotated left
